div.span: - This cache is shared by every user of that resolver, so a popular name is usually already there and steps 4 to 6 never run. On a miss the walk begins.

div.span: - This is the zone file you edit in BIND9 or in Route 53. It returns A 93.184.216.34 with a TTL of 300 seconds, and that TTL governs every cache downstream.

div.b: The answer travels back, caching as it goes

div.span: - The resolver stores the record for 300 seconds and replies to the client, which stores it too. Until that TTL expires, the same question is answered without a single packet leaving the machine.

div.b: Only now does the web request start

div.span: - Everything above happened before the first byte of HTTP. The browser opens the connection to the address it was given, and DNS plays no further part in it.

- The dashed green arrow is the resolved address returned to the client; the orange arrow is plain HTTP, no longer DNS.
